summary.text: A 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks and 6 days of gestation, with regular antenatal visits at a provincial hospital, presented to a tertiary care center for delivery. Five antenatal check-ups had consistently diagnosed placenta previa and transverse lie, and she had no abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding. At presentation she was in fair condition with stable vital signs and normal cardiopulmonary findings, and a fetal heart rate of 136 bpm.

Ultrasonography showed a single live fetus in transverse lie with an estimated gestational age of 36+6 weeks, fetal weight 2900 grams, adequate amniotic fluid and complete placenta previa. Per speculum examination showed a blood-stained cervix and no evidence of placenta previa, so a double setup examination was planned. Per vaginal examination found a 1 cm dilated cervix. Hemoglobin was 11.1 g/dl, blood group O positive, and other parameters were within normal limits.

An emergency cesarean section was planned due to the transverse lie in labor; she was counseled, consent was obtained and prophylactic antibiotics were given, and it was initiated under spinal anesthesia via a Pfannenstiel incision. An intact amniotic sac was found in the abdominal cavity with the placenta adhered to the greater omentum, left ovary and left fallopian tube; it was converted to general anesthesia and laparotomy. A live female neonate was delivered by breech extraction, and the placenta was separated and sent for histopathology.

Estimated blood loss was approximately 3500 ml; she received seven pints of whole blood, was transferred to the ICU, had an uneventful course and was discharged on the seventh postoperative day. The neonate, with APGAR scores of 4 and 6, was shifted to the NICU for poor respiratory effort and excessive greenish secretions and, despite intubation and oxygen therapy, died on the third day due to respiratory failure.

ambiguities.issue: Gestational age is stated as 39 weeks and 6 days (also 39+6 weeks in the abstract) while ultrasonography at presentation gave an estimated gestational age of 36+6 weeks; the source does not reconcile the two. The 39 weeks and 6 days figure is the gestation at presentation and 36+6 weeks is an ultrasonographic estimate, so they are different measurements rather than one conflicting value.
